source.title: Poco a Poco: An Elementary Direct Method for Learning Spanish
source.author: Guillermo F. Hall Avilés

lessons.title: Lección Primera
lessons.lede: The experiment begins with animals, size, direct questions and repeated model answers. Meaning is approached through Spanish before grammatical labels are introduced.
lessons.aim: Understand and answer the opening questions about animals, size, singular and plural
lessons.dayNote: Day 1. Excited. A little daunted. Why on earth did I challenge myself with this? Here goes… — A.W.P.G.
lessons.curiosityTitle: How much can you understand before translation?
lessons.curiosityText: Read the opening exchange in Lección Primera once without stopping. The repeated questions, answers and contrasts are designed to carry much of the meaning themselves.
lessons.curiositySample: El elefante es un animal. ¿Qué es el elefante? Es un animal.

readings.label: 1A
readings.title: Lección Primera: animales, tamaño y preguntas

studySteps.title: Read the original lesson
studySteps.text: Begin with Hall Avilés’ text and pictures. Read the complete lesson for sense before analysing individual forms.

studySteps.title: Write the key vocabulary
studySteps.text: Write each key Spanish word with its English equivalent, including the article with each noun.

studySteps.title: Write out the lesson
studySteps.text: Copy the story, conversation and exercises presented in the lesson by hand.

studySteps.title: Reread it aloud
studySteps.text: Read the complete lesson aloud, aiming for clarity and a steady natural rhythm rather than perfection.

studySteps.title: Mark and investigate difficulties
studySteps.text: Underline words you find difficult or do not understand, then look them up in a reliable Spanish dictionary.

checklist: Read Lección Primera in Poco a Poco
Listen to or make one complete reading
Write the key Spanish vocabulary and English equivalents
Write out the story, conversation and exercises
Look up those words in a dictionary
lessons.todaySpanish: The opening lesson demonstrates the direct method in miniature: meaning emerges through pictures, repetition, contrast and questions. The learner is already reading Spanish before receiving a formal grammar explanation.
lessons.notebookAlt: Alan’s handwritten notes for Lección Primera
lessons.notebookCaption: The notebook evidence for Lección Primera will be added after the complete reading, vocabulary, handwriting, speaking and dictionary work.

lessons.title: Lección Segunda
lessons.lede: The second lesson moves from animals to people and family. Juan, Antonio, María, Anita and Luisa introduce muchacho and muchacha, él and ella, ellos and ellas, and simple questions about brothers and sisters.
lessons.aim: Recognise and use basic words for boys, girls, brothers and sisters, together with él, ella, ellos and ellas
lessons.dayNote: Lesson 2. Familiar patterns, new people, and the first small step from naming things to describing relationships. — A.W.P.G.
lessons.curiosityTitle: How quickly do familiar question patterns carry new meaning?
lessons.curiosityText: Read the conversation once as a whole. Notice how the questions from Lección Primera now help you understand new words about people and family.
lessons.curiositySample: Juan es un muchacho. ¿Es María un muchacho? ¡Oh, no! Ella es una muchacha.

readings.label: 2A
readings.title: Lección Segunda: Juan, María y la familia

studySteps.title: Read the original lesson
studySteps.text: Read the complete conversation, practice material, useful phrases, exercise and questionnaire in Hall Avilés’ text.

studySteps.title: Write the key vocabulary
studySteps.text: Write each key Spanish word with its English equivalent, paying particular attention to muchacho, muchacha, hermano, hermana, él, ella, ellos and ellas.

studySteps.title: Write out the lesson
studySteps.text: Copy the story, conversation and exercises presented in Lección Segunda by hand.

studySteps.title: Reread it aloud
studySteps.text: Read the complete lesson aloud, keeping the questions and answers connected as a real exchange.

studySteps.title: Mark and investigate difficulties
studySteps.text: Underline words you find difficult or do not understand, then look them up in a reliable Spanish dictionary.

checklist: Read Lección Segunda in Poco a Poco
Listen to or make one complete reading

lessons.todaySpanish: Lección Segunda reuses the direct question-and-answer pattern while adding people, family relationships and personal pronouns. The familiar structure reduces the burden of the new vocabulary.
